rammedEarth.name: Rammed earth
rammedEarth.source: IS 3792:1978 Table 1 (rammed earth); ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals Ch. 26 Table 4 (earthen materials); solar absorptance/emissivity: BLUEPRINT.md Appendix B surface finish table
rammedEarth.blurb: Rammed earth: thick packed-earth walls, the classic heavy Ladakhi wall that stays warm all night.

mudPlaster.name: Mud plaster
mudPlaster.source: IS 3792:1978 Table 1 (mud plaster); solar absorptance/emissivity: BLUEPRINT.md Appendix B surface finish table
mudPlaster.blurb: Mud plaster: thin earthen render put over a wall, cheap and easy to redo every year.

timberPoplarWillow.name: Timber (poplar / willow)
timberPoplarWillow.source: IS 3629, Specification for structural timber in building; ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals Ch. 26 Table 4 (wood, softwood, low density). No dedicated finish-table row for bare wood; absorptance/emissivity are the ASHRAE Ch. 26 Table 14 default for a natural, unfinished wood surface.
timberPoplarWillow.blurb: Poplar and willow timber: locally grown, used for roof beams and lattice, insulates fairly well on its own.

gravelSoilFill.name: Gravel / soil fill
gravelSoilFill.source: IS 3792:1978 Table 1 (soil, gravel fill); ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals Ch. 26 Table 4 (soil).
gravelSoilFill.blurb: Gravel or soil fill: packed earth or stone chips under a floor, adds cheap mass that steadies the temperature.

singleGlazing.name: Single glazing
singleGlazing.source: BLUEPRINT.md Appendix B glazing table (U, SHGC, b0), compiled from ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals Ch. 15 (Fenestration) typical values per product class; tauVis has no source-document value; filled from typical NFRC-rated values for this glazing class, ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals Ch. 15 Table 4
singleGlazing.blurb: Single glazing: one sheet of glass, the cheapest window but loses heat fast.
